inputs.original_text: Bloomberg: “Every day, as energy prices rise, flights are canceled and death and destruction fill screens, people across the world ask when the Iran war — widely viewed as poorly planned, unwinnable and a peril to global well-being — will stop.” “Not in Israel, where the public is strongly behind seeing the war through until [...]
inputs.modified_text: Rising energy costs and canceled flights are hitting ordinary families, and leaders owe the public a clear account of what this war is meant to achieve and what risks they are asking people to bear. Support for Israel’s defense matters, but it is not a blank check for an open-ended conflict. National security requires resolve; it also requires competent leadership, defined aims, and accountability—not drifting into a war with no credible path to success.
